summary: The GAIA variant provides a robust implementation of the cockroach detection system using the SPADE multi-agent framework. It successfully implements all functional requirements, including sensor data collection, pattern recognition for hotspots, and multi-stakeholder notifications. However, it contains a critical security vulnerability due to the use of 'eval()' for message parsing.

findings.description: The system uses the unsafe 'eval()' function to parse message bodies in multiple agents (NotificationServiceAgent, BuildingAdministrationAgent, PestControlCompanyAgent, StudentResidentAgent). This allows for arbitrary code execution if an attacker can inject messages into the XMPP stream.
Excellent use of the SPADE framework to implement a truly distributed multi-agent system with clear role separation.
findings.evidence: mas_system.py: Use of spade.agent.Agent and Periodic/Cyclic behaviours.

findings.description: Fully addresses the requirement to identify hotspots and notify all required stakeholders (admin, pest control, students).
findings.evidence: mas_system.py: Implementation of NotificationServiceAgent that routes alerts to all three groups.

implementation_risks: Arbitrary code execution via malicious messages due to eval() usage.
